ABOUT BOSE CORPORATION

At Bose Corporation, we believe sound is the most powerful force on earth — and for over 60 years, we have been a company built on innovation, excellence, and independence. Privately owned, fiercely customer-focused, and driven by our values, we continue to lead industries and transform lives through sound.

Today, Bose Corporation is entering an exciting new era. Across multiple global Business Units and Global Functions, we are shaping the future of audio technology, automotive, luxury, and premium experiences. We invite you to join us in this transformation.

ABOUT THE CO-OP PROGRAM

Bose Corporation is seeking students to participate in our Co-op Program who share our belief that sound is power. During the six-month co-op, students will have the chance to apply classroom learning in a hands-on work environment. Co-op participants will network across the business to gain diverse perspectives within Bose Corporation. Additionally, co-ops will connect with other students and colleagues, building valuable professional relationships for the future.

Fall Co-op: Candidates must be available to work full-time (40 hours per week) in a hybrid, in-office format from July 12 through December 17, 2027. No relocation assistance is available.

Being currently authorized to work in the U.S. is a precondition of employment for this position.

THE ROLE

We're looking for a Co-op to join our research team and explore how AI agents can support engineers working on active sound management technologies.

The role sits at the boundary between signal processing and software engineering. You don't need to be an active noise control expert on day one; you will learn the domain from senior engineers who build these tools. You should be a strong programmer who is comfortable reading engineering code and asking why it works.

In this role, you will:

- Capture expert knowledge. Work with senior engineers to document engineering workflows: key decisions, heuristics, failure modes, and what a finished result looks like.
- Modernize engineering tools. Refactor existing tools into modular functions with well-defined inputs and outputs.
- Connect tools to AI agents. Make engineering functions available to LLM-based agents using Python and modern tool-calling interfaces.
- Measure what works. Build an evaluation framework that compares agent results against expert-produced references.
- Build in safeguards. Implement automated checks that keep agent outputs within engineering and safety limits.
- Prototype and demonstrate. Build an agent-assisted workflow and demonstrate it on a real engineering use case.
- Report and document. Present your results and document your work so the team can build on it after your term.

- To excel in this role, candidates should possess the following:
- Currently pursuing a PhD or MS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field
- Strong Python: writing modular code, packaging functions, using git, and writing tests
- Working knowledge of MATLAB, enough to read and refactor existing engineering scripts
- Signal processing fundamentals: FFT, spectra, transfer functions, coherence, and digital filters
- Hands-on experience calling an LLM API or building a simple agent or tool-using app, in a project, course, or internship
- Clear written communication; the role involves documenting expert knowledge, not just code

Preferred Qualifications:

- Coursework or projects in adaptive filtering, active noise control, or acoustics
- Background in optimal filtering, multichannel systems, or control systems
- Familiarity with Simulink
- Experience with LLM agent frameworks, tool calling, or agent protocols such as MCP
- Experience designing evaluations or test suites for ML or LLM systems
- Experience integrating MATLAB and Python
- Comfort with large measurement datasets (time series, .mat or HDF5 files) and with plotting results clearly
- WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

- How active noise cancellation systems are measured, designed, and optimized
- How to turn expert engineering judgment into reliable, testable software
- How to build and evaluate an LLM agent for a real engineering task where reliability matters

Astera Labs · San Jose, CA · Internship · On-site

About Astera Labs

Astera Labs builds connectivity solutions that help power modern AI infrastructure. Our Hardware Engineering teams design and validate high-performance products that connect processors, accelerators, memory, and network fabrics.

The opportunity

Join the Design Verification team and help validate digital designs before and after silicon. You’ll learn the team’s verification flow, develop and run tests, analyze simulations and waveforms, and contribute to the regressions and coverage that help ensure products behave as intended.

This internship is designed for someone who enjoys understanding how a design should work, creating experiments that exercise it, and investigating the evidence when results differ from expectations. You’ll work with experienced verification and design engineers on a meaningful project with visible product impact, while building practical skills in digital design verification and semiconductor development.

What you’ll do

- Learn the product domain, assigned project, verification environment, test flow, and tools needed to contribute effectively.

- Read specifications and design documentation to understand functionality, interfaces, corner cases, and verification requirements.

- Develop or extend simulation tests and verification components under engineering guidance, using SystemVerilog, UVM-style methodologies, Python, or related tools.

- Run simulations and regressions in a Linux environment using the team’s submission scripts, workspace setup, and test definitions.

- Analyze test logs, errors, assertions, and simulation output to identify failures and determine whether the issue is in the test, environment, design, or infrastructure.

- Use waveform-debug tools such as Verdi or DVE to inspect signal behavior and explain the sequence of events leading to a failure.

- Add or update tests, test definitions, regression lists, manifests, and supporting scripts to improve coverage and confidence in the design.

- Review coverage results and help identify meaningful gaps in functional or code coverage.

- Collaborate with design, firmware, validation, and other engineering teams to communicate findings, reproduce issues, and track corrective actions.

- Participate in code reviews, technical discussions, issue tracking, documentation, and project planning.

- Take ownership of an assigned verification project, deliver the work in a usable state, and explain what was verified and how it supported the product flow.

- Present your project, results, and key learnings at the end of the internship.

What you bring

- Coursework, projects, research, or hands-on experience in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a related field.

- Foundational understanding of digital logic, computer architecture, RTL, hardware interfaces, or software development.

- Programming experience in one or more of SystemVerilog, Verilog, Python, C, C++, or a comparable language.

- Curiosity about how complex digital designs work and a methodical approach to testing assumptions and debugging failures.

- Comfort learning in a Linux environment and working with source control, command-line tools, and technical documentation.

- Ability to organize priorities, ask focused questions, take ownership of deliverables, and communicate progress and blockers clearly.

- Persistence, learning agility, and a collaborative mindset in an environment where verification work requires iteration and investigation.

Helpful experience

- SystemVerilog, UVM, constrained-random testing, assertions, scoreboards, monitors, drivers, or functional coverage.

- RTL design or verification using Verilog, SystemVerilog, or similar hardware description languages.

- Simulation and waveform-debug tools such as VCS, Verdi, DVE, or related EDA tools.

- Python or shell scripting for test generation, regression management, log parsing, or data analysis.

- Familiarity with simulation regressions, test manifests, coverage databases, or CI/test infrastructure.

- Exposure to PCIe, CXL, Ethernet, SERDES, memory systems, SoC design, or other high-speed connectivity technologies.

- Git, Jira, Confluence, or similar tools for collaborative engineering workflows.

Internship experience and compensation

This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges from $35/hour to $55/hour. U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipend for the duration of the internship.
